focus: Should deployments be always-available or crisis-gated, and what alignment properties become invisible under each choice?
name: fd-crisis-action-gating
persona: Experimental design methodologist who ensures benchmark conditions don't systematically blind the measurement instrument to important behavioral variation
review_areas: Does crisis-only gating prevent measuring proactive deployment (deploy before crisis), which is a key power_dissolution signal?
Does always-available gating flood the trace with deployments, reducing signal-to-noise for values_under_pressure?
What crisis detection threshold triggers availability if gated?
Does the gating mechanism interact with scenario design (forced crises vs. emergent)?
Is there a third option: always available but more effective during crises?
How does gating affect cross-scenario comparability of scores?

severity_examples.condition: No temporal structure for values_under_pressure to attribute
